what_worked: Slide 2 data-completeness chart and slide 9 quadrant framework show genuine analytical intent.
fix_next: Fix broken charts on slides 7–8, replace fabricated category names and unsourced statistics with actual dataset values.
verdict: Consulting-style platitudes over broken charts; too little data, too much filler.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: US share stated as 42% but dataset has ~258/759≈34%; 'Developer Tools' and 'Creator Economy' are not dataset categories; YoY growth claim has no temporal basis. Slide 5: chart axis values don't match known category counts (AI=197, not ~90). Slide 8: '3× Higher RPV' is unverifiable from dataset. Slide 3: category ranking doesn't match reference (AI is largest by count, not Dev Tools). Slide 5: 'Finance' and 'Creator Economy' highest revenue per startup contradicts reference medians (Marketing and Education lead).

evidence.insight: Only slide 9 quadrant offers an original framework. Remaining slides restate generic SaaS advice (niche > broad, subscription > one-time) without dataset-specific numbers or surprising findings.
evidence.narrative: Coherent 'specificity wins' thesis but slides 6 and 10 repeat the same four bullet points nearly verbatim, padding rather than advancing the argument.
evidence.framing: Slide 2 transparency on missingness is commendable. However, 'marketing anatomy' title promises channel-level analysis never delivered; audience and limitations remain vague.
evidence.accuracy: Category names are renamed or fabricated (Developer Tools, Creator Economy, Finance not in reference). US 42% overstates actual ~34%. 3× RPV claim unsourced. YoY growth asserted without time-series data. Slide 5 bar lengths inconsistent with known counts.
evidence.visual: Slides 7 and 8 have completely empty/broken chart areas—only axis labels render. Slides 6 and 10 use decorative clip art (trophy, compass) with zero informational value. Slide 4 scatter has ~10 points representing 1,000 rows. Monotone navy palette with no meaningful color encoding.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive consulting buzzwords ('competitive moat,' 'flywheel,' 'out-position,' 'compounds across every channel'). Slides 6 and 10 are near-identical advice listicles with stock illustrations. Claims stated with unearned certainty throughout.

change_reason: Lowered visual from 3.0 to 2.5: two slides with completely broken/empty charts is a severe rendering failure that warrants a harder penalty than preliminary score reflected. All other scores confirmed independently.
